purpose: Canonical supplement of newly constituted authenticated hadith structures, distinct from historical H-ID recovery and reconstruction R-ID history.

identityPolicy.canonicalCountingRule: Each N-* structure counts +1 only after source verification and anti-duplication review; variants/parallels count +0.

canonicalStructures.theme: bienfaisance envers les parents — priorité de la mère puis du père
ḥayāʾ / pudeur comme partie de la foi
jeûne — protection et maîtrise du comportement
droits du musulman envers son frère
compassion mutuelle des croyants — image du corps
prise en charge de l’orphelin
soutien à la veuve et à la personne pauvre
canonicalStructures.narrator: Abu Huraira / transmission rapportée dans l’entrée

canonicalStructures.theme: rechercher ce qui est bénéfique, demander l’aide d’Allah et éviter le regret contrefactuel
mensonge, promesse rompue et trahison du dépôt — signes d’hypocrisie
témoignage d’Abu Sufyan devant Héraclius sur le Prophète ﷺ et les caractéristiques de son appel
dignité humaine — condamner l’insulte liée aux origines et traiter équitablement ceux sous sa responsabilité
foi — même une quantité infime de foi est reconnue dans le hadith
hadith de Jibril — Islam, foi, iḥsān et signes de l’Heure
visite au malade — rester dans le verger du Paradis jusqu’au retour
aumône, pardon et humilité — la richesse ne diminue pas par l’aumône, le pardon élève et l’humilité pour Allah élève
intercéder en faveur d’une personne dans le besoin afin d’aider à l’obtention d’un bien
voie vers le Paradis — adoration d’Allah sans association, prière, zakat et maintien des liens de parenté
priorité des œuvres — prière à son heure, bonté envers les parents puis effort dans la voie d’Allah
pensées involontaires — pardon tant qu’elles ne sont ni prononcées ni mises en acte
plantation utile — ce qu’un humain ou un animal en mange est compté comme aumône
dhikr — subḥān Allāh, al-ḥamdu lillāh, lā ilāha illa Allāh et Allāhu akbar, plus aimés que ce sur quoi le soleil se lève
invocation enseignée — pardon, miséricorde, guidée et subsistance
canonicalStructures.narrator: Abu Malik al-Ashja'i, from his father

canonicalStructures.theme: serviteur croyant — double récompense lorsqu’il sert loyalement son maître et adore correctement son Seigneur
dhikr après la prière — tasbih, tahmid et takbir trente-trois fois, puis tahlil pour compléter cent
invocation de protection — chercher refuge contre l’épreuve difficile, le malheur, le mauvais destin et la joie malveillante des ennemis

referenceCorrection.reason: Le thème et le matn identifient l’invocation d’Abu Huraira contre l’épreuve difficile, le malheur, le mauvais destin et la joie malveillante des ennemis.

canonicalStructures.theme: invocation de pardon — demander pardon pour faute, ignorance, excès et ce qu’Allah connaît mieux
invocation avant le sommeil — Seigneur des cieux et de la terre, protection contre le mal de toute créature
vérité dans la parole conduisant à la droiture, et mensonge conduisant à la perversité
responsabilité confiée à chacun — chacun est gardien et responsable de ce qui lui est confié
affaire du croyant — gratitude dans l’aisance et patience dans l’épreuve
récitation du Qur’an — il viendra intercéder pour ses compagnons au Jour de la Résurrection
Allah est Bon et n’accepte que ce qui est bon; lien entre nourriture/gain licites et invocation
réparer une injustice envers autrui avant le Jour de la Résurrection
Allah divided mercy into one hundred parts, kept ninety-nine with Him, and sent one part to earth; creation shows mercy through that one part
Allah's mercy predominates His wrath
Allah says that He is as His servant thinks of Him and is with the servant when the servant remembers Him
The most superior way of asking Allah for forgiveness; the narration also states the consequence for one who says it with firm faith and dies before evening or morning.
Supplication asking Allah to set right one's religion, worldly life and Hereafter, to make life an increase in good and death a relief from evil.
A desert Arab is taught words of glorification, then a personal supplication for pardon, mercy, guidance and sustenance.
canonicalStructures.narrator: Mus'ab bin Sa'd, on the authority of his father

canonicalStructures.theme: Supplication seeking refuge from incapacity, sloth, cowardice, miserliness, decrepitude and grave torment; asking for the soul's righteousness and purification; seeking refuge from useless knowledge, an unhumble heart, an unsatisfied soul and an unanswered supplication.
The Prophet instructs Ali to ask Allah for guidance and adherence to the straight path, illustrating guidance by the road and rectitude by the straightness of an arrow.
The Prophet teaches istikhara for matters: two non-obligatory units of prayer followed by a supplication entrusting knowledge, power, outcome and contentment to Allah.
Responding to an objectionable act according to ability: by hand, then tongue, then rejection in the heart, the last being the weakest degree of faith.
canonicalStructures.narrator: Tariq bin Shihab, reporting Abu Sa'id

canonicalStructures.theme: A man visits a brother solely out of love for Allah; an angel tells him that Allah loves him as he loves his brother for Allah's sake.
Faith and mutual love are linked, and spreading the greeting of peace among people is taught as a means of fostering that love.

Hadith qudsi forbidding oppression; servants are directed to ask Allah for guidance, food, clothing and forgiveness; human piety or wickedness does not change Allah's dominion, and deeds are recorded and recompensed.
Hadith qudsi warning against hostility to a devoted servant; nearness to Allah begins with obligations and continues through voluntary deeds until divine love, protection and answered supplication.
The world is described as a prison for the believer and a paradise for the non-believer.
Supplication is granted so long as the supplicant does not become impatient and say that the supplication was not answered.
Whoever takes people's money intending repayment receives Allah's aid in repaying it, while one who takes it intending destruction is destroyed by Allah.
A man who had killed one hundred people set out toward a place of repentance, died on the way, and was forgiven after being found closer to the destination of reform.
After a person's death, deeds end except for recurring charity, beneficial knowledge, or a righteous child who supplicates for the deceased.
One who guides another person to a good action receives a reward similar to the reward of its doer.
Convey the Prophet's teaching even if only one statement; narrating reports from the Children of Israel is permitted, while deliberate lying about the Prophet incurs a warning of the Fire.
Supplication asking Allah for right guidance, piety and protection from evil, chastity, and freedom from want.
Stages of human creation in the womb, the angel's writing of deeds, livelihood, lifespan and final state, and the warning that a person's concluding deeds may differ from earlier conduct.
When given a choice, the Prophet chose the easier permissible option; he was farthest from sin and did not take personal revenge unless Allah's sacred limits were violated.
Seven categories of people granted shade by Allah on the Day when there is no other shade.
Spending on one’s family while seeking Allah’s reward is counted as charity.
The most hated person in Allah’s sight is the most obstinately quarrelsome person.
Allah has not created a disease without also creating its treatment.
On the Day of Resurrection, neglecting to visit a sick servant or provide food or drink is confronted through the reward that would have been found with Allah.
Allah has prepared for His righteous servants in Paradise what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived.
Allah has prescribed excellence in all things; killing and slaughter must be done well, with a sharpened blade and comfort for the animal.
The best food is that earned through one’s own manual work; Prophet David ate from his manual earnings.
The recipient and payer of interest, its recorder, and its two witnesses are all included in the same condemnation.
All followers of the Prophet will enter Paradise except those who refuse; obeying him leads to Paradise, while disobeying him constitutes refusal.
A man gave water to a very thirsty dog, and Allah accepted the deed and forgave him; there is a reward for serving every living creature.
One Umra to the next expiates the sins committed between them, and an accepted Hajj has no reward other than Paradise.
A good companion and a bad companion are compared to a musk seller and a bellows blower: one brings benefit or a pleasant scent, while the other may burn clothes or leave a bad smell.

The gates of Paradise are opened on Mondays and Thursdays and forgiveness is granted to those who do not associate partners with Allah, except two people at enmity, whose case is deferred until they reconcile.
